meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Daniel Lee (Celestia Head of Partnerships), Rita Gomez (Celestia SE), Marco Silva (Celestia Cloud Solutions)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Celestia Compute. Primary focus: partner integration model (cloud + GPU hardware), technical compatibility for private/dedicated deployments, go-to-market motions and revenue share. Celestia interested in bundling Redwood inference as a managed option on their GPU cloud; key asks: integration effort, security/compliance posture, perf benchmarks, and pricing alignments.
topics: Hardware mapping: GPUs, drivers, and quantization support
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate the intro Daniel. Quick roll call?
00:07 Daniel (Celestia): Yeah hi, Daniel here, thanks Alex. We've got Rita and Marco on, I'll hand over to them in a sec.
00:13 Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya from Redwood, I'll be the SE on any technical follow ups.
:--
01:05 Daniel (Celestia): Super, goal for us is to see how Redwood might fit into our marketplace offering — we run GPU clusters across EU and NA, lots of customers asking for a managed inference stack.
01:18 Rita (Celestia): To add, we do both preemptible and reserved pools, and we are exploring partners for model serving and a vendor that can help with both hosted and private options.
01:30 Alex (Redwood): Great. At a high level Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity and private deployments. Our partner program has options to bundle hosted credits or co-sell dedicated capacity.
01:47 Marco (Celestia): Nice. A couple of immediate questions: what GPU types do you typically support, and how much lift for private/on-prem customers?
02:02 Priya (Redwood SE): We support a wide range — A100, H100, and combinations — and our runtime picks kernels and quantization paths depending on architecture. For private deployments we provide a control plane that can be customer-managed, plus an on-prem package for air-gapped.
02:21 Daniel (Celestia): When you say "control plane" is that fully in-customer VPC? We need to understand network patterns — many of our customers require no egress for model inputs.
02:33 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we offer a private control plane that is deployed into customer VPCs or on-prem; you can keep inference plane isolated. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management and support SSO/SAML and RBAC. (small pause) There's occasionally some doc that calls it Redwood Privet in notes, sorry for the typo.
02:55 Marco (Celestia): Good. On licensing, are partners able to resell Redwood Dedicated as a managed add-on?
03:08 Alex (Redwood): Yes — partner resale and co-sell are both options. We have a partner-tier program with revenue share for dedicated capacity, and an API-based hosted referral model for lower-touch integrations. We'll send the partner deck after.
03:25 Rita (Celestia): Great, please include any pricing guidance for 24/7 reserved pools versus bursty preemptible style.
03:32 Alex (Redwood): Will do. Also can you share typical workload shapes? Are customers latency sensitive real-time chat or large-batch embeddings?
03:45 Daniel (Celestia): A mix — chat for SMB apps (low latency) and batch embeddings for analytics. We're seeing a spike in cost concerns so anyone who can optimize token-cost is interesting.
04:02 Priya (Redwood SE): Our Optimize toolkit helps with batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions; we also have quality monitoring to track regressions when switching quantized models.
04:16 Marco (Celestia): On the tech side, what's the integration surface? Do you offer a Kubernetes operator or is it API-first?
04:27 Priya (Redwood SE): API-first for hosted, but for dedicated/private we provide deployment manifests, helm charts and a lightweight operator. Many partners run our runtime inside their infra.
04:40 Daniel (Celestia): Any special driver/kernel support? We've had issues with CUDA versions and custom AMIs in the past.
04:49 Priya (Redwood SE): We maintain tested stacks for common CUDA/toolkit versions; runtime can operate on top of vendor drivers. For especially custom kernels we can coordinate with your infra team — sometimes labels get messy in transcription, the term K V cash was used in another call — we mean KV cache.
05:05 Alex (Redwood): Quick question on go-to-market: what's Celestia's ideal partner motion? Marketplace listing, resell, or managed offering?
05:16 Daniel (Celestia): Marketplace and co-managed offering is preferred—customers like turnkey options. Resell is okay but we'd prefer a default package to reduce friction.
05:25 Alex (Redwood): Makes sense. We'll propose a 3-tier partner flow: reference integration, managed offering with revenue share, and full white-label private deployments.
05:36 Rita (Celestia): For the managed offering, how much onboarding effort should we expect? A ballpark for a single node cluster?
05:45 Priya (Redwood SE): For a basic integration and a single-node test cluster, 2-3 engineer-days for configuration and validation; for production dedicated clusters expect 2-4 weeks depending on network and compliance requirements.
06:02 Marco (Celestia): That helps. About benchmarks — our engineering team will want to run performance tests. Do you provide benchmark scripts or a harness?
06:12 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes we have a benchmark checklist and harness. We'll share a lightweight workload template; you can mirror our sequence length profiles and model variants. We can also run a co-benchmark if you provide access to a sample cluster.
06:28 Daniel (Celestia): We can provision a small sandbox cluster. Would you need S3 buckets or anything special?
06:35 Priya (Redwood SE): S3 or object storage for model artifacts is typical. For private pilots we can also accept OCI images and model blobs.
06:45 Alex (Redwood): On security, do you need our SOC2 and architecture docs? Celestia will likely ask for them for enterprise customers.
06:53 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — we'll share SOC2, our data retention policy, audit logs features, and KMS integration docs. Also we have optional EKM/HSM integrations.
07:05 Rita (Celestia): Wonderful. On multi-region: we operate EU and NA, some APAC via partners. Is Redwood okay with multi-region routing and fallbacks?
07:16 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — smart routing is a core feature, we can route by latency, cost, or region, and set fallback policies. For regulatory workloads you can pin models to regions.
07:29 Marco (Celestia): A specific customer ask — low-evidence medical transcription — they require no PHI egress, is on-prem only. Can Redwood support air-gapped on-prem?
07:42 Alex (Redwood): Yes, we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments; integration effort depends on networking and key management.
07:52 Daniel (Celestia): Any requirements on GPU families for quantized models? We're trying to understand where H100 is necessary vs A100 or even consumer-grade options for certain smaller models.
08:08 Priya (Redwood SE): Quantization profiles vary; H100 helps with throughput for large decoder models but we can run smaller quantized models on A100 or T4 in some cases. We'll provide model-specific guidance.
08:22 Alex (Redwood): Let's talk about partner economics — does Celestia have preferred revenue share or margins?
08:32 Daniel (Celestia): We generally do 70/30 partner split for infrastructure resell but are open to discussion depending on co-marketing and pipeline commitments.
08:42 Alex (Redwood): Noted. We'll outline tiered options.
09:00 (short cross-talk)
10:10 Priya (Redwood SE): Technical note: our serving runtime supports continuous batching, KV cache, and kernel selection based on model arch. Some customers see 20-40% cost improvement after tuning.
10:28 Rita (Celestia): That's compelling. One practical item: do you have a partner API key flow for marketplace listings? We prefer ephemeral keys per customer.
10:38 Alex (Redwood): We support scoped API keys and partner tokens; ephemeral keys are doable for marketplace provisioning.
10:47 Marco (Celestia): Any SLA for dedicated pools?
10:52 Alex (Redwood): For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in contract. We'll share sample SLA language.
11:05 Daniel (Celestia): On compliance, can Redwood sign data processing addendums that align with GDPR and data residency constraints?
11:15 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, DPA and BAA are possible; we also provide audit logging for requests and optional masked logs.
11:28 Alex (Redwood): Great. Quick operational question — how do we surface per-tenant cost breakdowns into a partner's billing console?
11:38 Priya (Redwood SE): We can expose token-level cost, per-route usage, and tagging to map to Celestia customer IDs. Partners can consume telemetry via our billing API or push to a partner-owned reporting endpoint.
12:00 Marco (Celestia): Perfect. I'd like to go deeper — driver mismatches and kernel bugs are a real source of pain. Could we set up a technical deep dive with our infra team next week?
12:12 Priya (Redwood SE): Absolutely. We'll coordinate — propose next Thu/Fri.
12:20 Daniel (Celestia): Also we'd like to see a reference deployment or case study for a cloud partner.
12:28 Alex (Redwood): We'll send a partner case study and reference contacts.
12:34 (brief pause)
15:00 Alex (Redwood): Heading into some more detailed Q&A — runbook questions, provisioning, monitoring...
15:18 Rita (Celestia): How does Redwood handle model rollouts and canarying?
15:24 Priya (Redwood SE): We support canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to compatible variants. Rollouts are configurable per-route.
15:36 Marco (Celestia): If we want to offer Redwood as an add-on in our console, what's the provisioning flow for end-customers?
15:45 Alex (Redwood): Typically marketplace flows provision an API token and a minimal config; for managed offerings there's a provisioning playbook and a handoff to a solutions engineer.
16:01 Daniel (Celestia): Anything that would block us from running a pilot in 2-3 weeks?
16:09 Priya (Redwood SE): Only things like legal sign-off and access to a sandbox cluster. For basic benchmark we just need a small node and object storage.
16:18 Alex (Redwood): We'll include a pilot checklist in the follow-up.
18:00 Rita (Celestia): On observability, can we pull traces into our APM?
18:08 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes we have tracing hooks and per-route dashboards; we can send logs or metrics to external endpoints.
18:20 Marco (Celestia): For billing, can we get per-tenant tagging to pass through to our cost reports?
18:28 Alex (Redwood): Yes, tagging and token attribution supported.
20:00 (short mid-call summary)
20:12 Alex (Redwood): Recap — we'll send partner deck, benchmark checklist, SOC2 and DPA docs, propose dates for technical deep dive and pilot.
20:25 Daniel (Celestia): That covers our needs. One more question: do you support model quantization tools in the partner toolkit or do partners handle quantization?
20:36 Priya (Redwood SE): We provide quantization guidance and profiles; partners typically run quantization with our recommended tooling, but we can assist for first-time setups.
23:00 Marco (Celestia): On billing again — any minimum commitments for dedicated?
23:10 Alex (Redwood): Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts; minimums vary by region but we'll share ranges in the partner deck.
25:40 Rita (Celestia): Legal will want our standard contract redline — can Redwood legal review partner SOWs?
25:50 Alex (Redwood): Yes, our legal team will. We'll need to see the draft.
27:00 Priya (Redwood SE): Technical ask: please capture the model families you run and the expected seq lengths so we can map kernels appropriately.
27:12 Marco (Celestia): We'll share that.
28:00 (brief cross-talk)
30:00 Alex (Redwood): Anything else from Celestia?
30:10 Daniel (Celestia): Not for now — next steps and docs are most important.
30:20 Alex (Redwood): Great. We'll follow up with materials and schedule the deep dive.
31:00 (closing remarks)
47:30 End of meeting.
